name: Relay simulation causal chain (M1 -> M2 -> M3 with SFI physical constraint)
description: Operationalises the paper's three-stage relay topology under the Signal Fidelity Inequality (Eq. 6). The operator-controllable M2 residence time tau_m2_h, combined with literature-estimated k_decay and the initial signal pool s0, determines whether the relay completes within its physical horizon. This DAG identifies tau_m2_h -> final_ser through the signal-activity decay path, with k_decay_point and s0 as critical confounders.
paper_reference: BOS_Paper1_JCP_FINAL.docx — paper line 51-54 (Eq. 5: S(tau) = S_0 * exp(-k_decay*tau), Eq. 6: tau_M2 <= ln(S_0/S_min)/k_decay); §4.1 (mechanistic basis of the engineered relay, claim #16 in reconnaissance §3.1: 'The cue reduces the activation inertia of the successor stage'); §3.6.1 M1/M2/M3 progressive covariate adjustment.
node_id_convention: Causal-semantic IDs; see bos_field_ref for schema field mapping. Time-indexed via @step_at_<phase>_<position> DSL (e.g. @step_at_m3_boundary).

nodes.description: M2 stage residence time [h]. Operator-controlled scheduling parameter (Eq. 5 exposure time).
Initial signal-activity pool [BU-equivalent units]. Operator-set at M2 onset. Combined with k_decay determines physical horizon tau_max (Eq. 6).
First-order signal decay rate [1/h] (Eq. 5-6). Literature-estimated per paper §SFI honesty rule — the schema makes this provenance-tagged.
Eq. 6 physical horizon tau_max = ln(s0/s_min)/k_decay [h]. Mediates between (tau_m2_h, k_decay, s0) and final_ser via the SFI feasibility gate.
Terminal signal activity at M2 boundary, S(tau_m2_h) = s0 * exp(-k_decay * tau_m2_h) (Eq. 5). Carries the dose-time-integrated potency into M3.
Larval biomass at M3 start [kg]. Downstream of M2 priming. Drives subsequent N assimilation.
Residual substrate at M3 start [kg]. Inversely related to D' through Eq. 1.
Insect species. Stratum-level confounder; affects biomass growth response to primed substrate.
Relay-final SER [0, 1]. The endpoint that integrates M1-M2-M3 performance.
Aggregate relay health verdict (nominal / degraded / failed). Auxiliary outcome; failure path activates when tau_m2_h > tau_max_h.

edges.paper_quote: S(tau) = S_0 * exp(-k_decay * tau) (Eq. 5) — exposure time enters the exponent.

tau_M2 <= ln(S_0/S_min)/k_decay — violation of this inequality triggers the relay_health failure path (paper §SFI honesty rule operationalised in schemas/relay.py RelayHealth.k_decay_violation_at_step).

intended_question: What is the average causal effect of M2 residence time tau_m2_h on final_ser, controlling for k_decay (literature-estimated, confounder) and species_code (stratum)? Also: when tau_m2_h approaches tau_max_h, how sharply does relay_health_status flip from 'nominal' to 'failed'? Identifies via back-door adjustment on {k_decay_point, s0, species_code}.
estimator_recommendation: LinearDML for the main tau_m2_h -> final_ser effect. The discontinuity at tau_max_h is a Regression Discontinuity candidate (DoWhy's regression_discontinuity_estimator) but Phase B MVP keeps it simple — RDD is reserved for Phase-B-2.
small_sample_warning: Paper line 99 reports M3 simulation interval crosses zero at n=4 ('under-determined covariate design at n=4'). DAG 003's identifiability is tighter than DAG 001's because tau_m2_h is operator-set (so we have within-arm variation if multiple tau_m2_h values are tested), but the n-floor still bites for the heterogeneity-stratified version. Phase B will auto-clamp evidence_level on this DAG identically to DAG 001 / 002.
notes_for_user_review: DAG 003 is the most physics-grounded of the three (every paper-edge is an explicit equation). The two 'domain' edges (biomass_kg_m3 / substrate_kg_m3 -> final_ser) are mechanical bridges between the relay simulation outputs and the SER definition; they are formally derivable from Eq. 1-3 once you accept the chain dm_in -> dm_out via substrate_kg trajectory. The Regression Discontinuity opportunity at tau_max_h is flagged but deferred.
